title: Plug a keyed ribbon cable connector onto a sensor board while holding its stand
instruction: Plug the ribbon cable into the green sensor board. Pick the cable's black connector up from the tray by its two ends, turn it so the raised key on its side lines up with the notch in the wall of the black box header near the board's free end, lower it straight into the header and press it firmly down until it gives and seats fully. The board sticks out past the end of the orange stand's foot, so pressed on its own the stand tips over: hold the stand down with one hand, pressing straight down on the black rubber pad on the block at its left end, while you press with the other. Let go once the connector is in.
context: Plugging keyed ribbon cables onto box headers is one of the most common steps in wiring sensors, motor drivers and robot electronics, and a connector that is half seated or forced in the wrong way round makes the board fail. Robots that can do it can help wire up more robots.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward, y to the robots' left. Sensor board on its stand, one loose body, 55 g in all, its weight 8.5 cm behind the foot's right end. Stand: orange PLA, 40 mm wide (x 0.280 to 0.320), lying along y: a flat foot 5 mm thick from y -0.040 to 0.140; on its left end a block 3 cm long, top 2.5 cm above the table, with a black rubber press pad 24 x 24 x 1 mm centred at (0.30, 0.125); on its right end a riser 3.5 cm long (y -0.040 to -0.005), top 2 cm above the table, with two brass standoffs 5 mm across and 5 mm tall at (0.281, -0.016) and (0.319, -0.016). Board: green FR4, 50 x 80 x 1.6 mm (x 0.275 to 0.325, y -0.090 to -0.010), screwed on the standoffs, underside 2.5 cm above the table, so 5 cm of it sticks out past the foot's right end; a black chip 6 x 6 x 1 mm on it at (0.30, -0.050). Header: black plastic shrouded 2 x 5 pin box header centred at (0.30, -0.08), 19.6 mm along x, 11.6 mm along y, 7 mm tall above the board, with a 1 mm floor and 1.2 mm walls round a cavity 17.2 x 9.2 mm; a key slot 5 mm wide through the middle of its -y wall, facing the board's free edge. Inside it a black contact plate with the 10 gold pin tips (2 rows of 5, 2.54 mm pitch along x), 4 mm above the board; it gives once pressed 1 mm (5 N) and then sinks 2.5 mm. White tape outline 3 mm wide on the table, its inner edges 2 mm outside the foot (x 0.278 and 0.322, y -0.042 and 0.142). Tray, fixed: aluminium 60 x 60 x 4 mm centred at (0.22, -0.20). Connector, loose, 4 g: black plastic IDC socket 16 x 8 x 11 mm with a key 3.5 mm wide and 2 mm proud running its full height in the middle of one long side, and a stub of grey ribbon cable 12.7 mm wide, 1 mm thick and 12 mm long standing up from the middle of its top, a red stripe on one edge. It stands on its underside centred on the tray, its length along y, key facing -x, towards the robots. No other objects.
scoring: Measured once everything has come to rest, relative to the board. 0 if any corner of the stand's foot is more than 10 mm from where it started (the tape outline shows it) or the stand is tilted more than 15 degrees. Otherwise the connector is in the header if the centre of its underside is within 1.5 mm of the header's centre, it is tilted no more than 10 degrees from the board's vertical, and its underside is no more than 6 mm above the board's top (at least 1 mm below the top of the header's walls). 0 if it is not in the header. 0.25 if it is in the header but not seated. 1.0 if it is seated, its underside at most 2 mm above the board's top (within 0.5 mm of its seat at 1.5 mm), with its key in the header's slot. Unpressed, it rests 4 mm above the board; the wrong way round, its key sits on the header's wall, 7 mm above the board.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Pull the connector out and stand it on the tray, key towards the robots, and set the stand flat inside its tape outline. In simulation the press fit is restored at each reset.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX at 240 Hz. The connector is a solid block and the pins are not contacts: it rests on a sprung plate in the header that stands in for the pins' insertion force, gives at 5 N and lets it sink 2.5 mm to its seat, where it stays. Clearances are 0.6 mm with no chamfers. The ribbon is a short rigid stub, not a flexible cable. The stand, board and header are one body of uniform density.
